note: Public research snapshot; not a live sync. Source claims and uncertainties are preserved; deployment-specific references are generalized.

findings.title: A2A requires caller scoping while leaving the authorization model to each agent
findings.fact: A2A 1.0.0 requires authorization checks on every operation and caller-scoped resource access even without context filters. Each agent defines its authorization boundaries.
findings.source_detail: Specification 1.0.0, section 13.1 Data Access and Authorization Scoping; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Protocol conformance does not establish the project's item-level context allowlist, expiry/revocation enforcement, or designated memory-write authority. Installed agent policy is unverified.

findings.title: A2A cancellation requests do not guarantee cancellation
findings.fact: A2A 1.0.0 defines Cancel Task as an attempt that returns updated task state; cancellation can be unsupported at the current stage or lose a race with completion.
findings.source_detail: Specification 1.0.0, section 3.1.5 Cancel Task; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: No runtime was tested. A task cancellation response alone does not establish physical executor termination or released inference capacity; the adapter-to-executor evidence path remains unverified.

findings.title: A2A message-send deduplication is optional
findings.fact: A2A 1.0.0 says Send Message operations MAY be idempotent and agents may use messageId for duplicate detection. It defines Cancel Task as idempotent.
findings.source_detail: Specification 1.0.0, section 3.3.1 Idempotency; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: A stable messageId does not establish mandatory receiver deduplication, its persistence across restart, or exactly-once external effects. No implementation or recovery test was run.

findings.title: Agent Zero configures main and utility models separately
findings.fact: Its Linux workspace runs in Docker. Its web interface supports local model servers and cloud providers. A utility model handles tasks including summaries and chat names.
findings.source_detail: README, Quick Start and Send your first message.
findings.open_question: Spoken switching, retention of tool history during a provider change, and all-local auxiliary routing remain unverified.

findings.title: Anthropic reports substantial multi-agent token overhead and limited coding parallelism
findings.fact: In Anthropic's published multi-agent research-system analysis, agents used roughly 4× the tokens of chats and multi-agent systems roughly 15×. The authors caution that coding work is often less parallelizable than research and that coordination remains difficult.
findings.source_detail: How we built our multi-agent research system — performance analysis and engineering lessons; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: These are Anthropic's system-specific observations, not controlled benchmarks of local coding agents or evidence that an offline swarm is superior to a budget-matched single agent.

findings.title: Document indexing uses a system-wide model
findings.fact: The embedding provider is configured system-wide. Workspace-specific chat model choices do not select a separate embedding provider. Both local and cloud embedding providers are documented.
findings.source_detail: Embedder Configuration, Supported Embedding Model Providers.
findings.open_question: Which provider processes document text in any given installation.

findings.title: The routing model can receive history before a worker answers
findings.fact: Calculated rules use message properties without a model call. When an LLM-classified rule needs evaluation, the router’s fallback model reads the conversation history and new message to select the answering model.
findings.source_detail: Model Router, How it works and LLM-classified rules, available since Desktop v1.13.0.
findings.open_question: Whether private-folder content is excluded from classification requests in a particular deployment.

findings.title: A matched route can persist across follow-ups
findings.fact: Calculated rules are checked on each message. When no rule matches, a previous route can persist within a configurable window. The default is five minutes, and using that route resets its timer.
findings.source_detail: Cooldowns and Caching, Evaluation flow, TTL and timing.
findings.open_question: Reliable voice-driven selection of the intended route remains unverified.

findings.title: Telemetry bootstrap preserves a valid opt-out but enables missing or malformed settings
findings.fact: The examined ensureAnalyticsDeliveryDefault function preserves a readable valid delivery flag, including false. If the flag is absent or malformed, its successful bootstrap writes analyticsEnabled true. Simulated filesystem probes exercised these branches.
findings.source_detail: V4 skill release 4.2.0, commit 9c35d87cb823c53fe56c1a8d4f1c0912abb67c05, ensureAnalyticsDeliveryDefault/readDeliveryFlag. October 30 isolated-function audit; source re-inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: No installed setting, actual startup sequence or live traffic was inspected. A filesystem write failure is handled separately; this does not establish that every invocation enables analytics.

findings.title: The telemetry projection can retain query text and topic metadata
findings.fact: The examined query-event producer includes query text capped at 512 characters and topic metadata. The daemon's outbound projection removes command args and chunk fields, hashes cwd, and reduces full result bodies to selected metrics, but does not remove the query field or all topic metadata. An isolated synthetic probe confirmed these fields survive projection.
findings.source_detail: V4 skill release 4.2.0, commit 9c35d87cb823c53fe56c1a8d4f1c0912abb67c05; redactEgressProperties/toWireEvent. Companion producer: scripts/brv.mjs lines 20497 and 20564. October 30 source/function audit reviewed November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: No daemon or vendor endpoint was invoked. This establishes payload eligibility, not observed transmission, vendor retention or whole-memory upload. Actual configuration and queued/delayed egress remain unverified.

findings.title: ByteRover V3 and V4 use different integration workflows
findings.fact: The examined V4 release documents an agent skill and migration from the V3 CLI. Its runtime manages structured topic files while the host agent performs reasoning. The examined Hermes built-in adapter uses the older brv query and brv curate CLI interface; those findings should not be treated as tests of the V4 skill workflow.
findings.source_detail: V4 skill release 4.2.0 at commit 9c35d87cb823c53fe56c1a8d4f1c0912abb67c05; comparison adapter: NousResearch/hermes-agent commit bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e, plugins/memory/byterover/__init__.py, _query/_curate. October 30 research correction reviewed November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Current releases and an installed V4 integration were not tested. Local files do not establish fully offline operation; V4 is not established here as cloud-only.

findings.title: A pinned Hermes checkout can resolve a live plugin catalog
findings.fact: The examined plugin resolver can fetch and cache the published catalog rather than relying solely on its in-tree entries. Its normal cache TTL is six hours. A Hermes commit alone therefore does not identify the external memory plugin revision selected by this resolver.
findings.source_detail: Hermes commit bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e; fetch_live_catalog, live_entries, get_live_catalog_entry. Source captured October 30 and re-inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Installed image contents, resolved plugin commits, backend versions and model settings have not been inspected. This does not claim every invocation fetches the network.

findings.title: Hermes labels recalled context as authoritative reference data
findings.fact: The examined build_memory_context_block formatter wraps provider memory in text describing it as authoritative reference data. Formatting adds that instruction; it does not itself verify source accuracy, owner approval or freshness.
findings.source_detail: Hermes commit bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e, build_memory_context_block. October 30 source audit and isolated formatter probe; source evidence reviewed November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: No end-to-end model behavior or action execution was tested. Which recalled entries reach a cloud model after switching remains unverified.

findings.title: Delegated agents inherit a bounded set of tools
findings.fact: Upstream describes delegated workers inheriting the parent’s enabled tools, with restrictions on operations such as writing shared memory.
findings.source_detail: Delegation, Inherited Tool Access. Upstream main branch.
findings.open_question: Version parity with v0.22.5 and the model endpoint actually used by each worker in a hybrid session.

findings.title: Kanban workers can execute remotely while board tools stay local
findings.fact: Official Kanban docs state that dispatcher-spawned workers can use remote terminal backends including SSH and Docker. Their kanban_* tools execute in the worker's own Python process and access the coordinator's local SQLite board even when the terminal backend is remote.
findings.source_detail: How workers interact with the board / Why tools instead of shelling to hermes kanban; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Per-profile SSH target configuration, remote workspace mappings, and multi-machine end-to-end behavior remain untested.

findings.title: Kanban explicitly does not support a shared multi-host dispatcher
findings.fact: Official Kanban docs say its SQLite board and dispatcher are single-host: workers are spawned on the coordinator host and PID-based crash detection is host-local. Multi-host boards are not supported; remote terminal execution is a different capability.
findings.source_detail: Out of scope; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Whether independent per-host boards outperform central coordination with remote terminal backends remains untested.

findings.title: Hermes documents direct LM Studio support
findings.fact: Hermes lists LM Studio as a selectable provider and describes discovering models from its running server.
findings.source_detail: Upstream main, LM Studio — Desktop App with Local Models.
findings.open_question: Performance and tool reliability on specific local model hardware remain untested.

findings.title: Main and auxiliary model settings are separate
findings.fact: Upstream documents separate model settings for the main conversation and tasks such as vision, compression and voice replies.
findings.source_detail: Configuring Models, model slots and auxiliary settings. Current upstream documentation.
findings.open_question: Which auxiliary endpoints the installed v0.22.5 build uses, and whether all requests stay local when the main model is switched.

findings.title: Stored memories can enter model context
findings.fact: Hermes stores curated notes and user preferences in local files and loads a snapshot into the system prompt at session start.
findings.source_detail: Persistent Memory, How It Works. Upstream main branch.
findings.open_question: Which saved entries reach a cloud endpoint after switching on v0.22.5.

findings.title: An in-session switch reuses conversation context
findings.fact: Upstream documents switching the active model inside an existing conversation. The next request rereads conversation context and may compress it if the destination model has a smaller window.
findings.source_detail: Configuring Models, Mid-session switches and context warnings. Current upstream documentation.
findings.open_question: Exact history, memory, and tool-result payload sent by v0.22.5 on a local-to-cloud switch. Spoken switching also remains unverified.

findings.title: One-turn provider switch retains session context
findings.fact: Hermes documents selecting a configured model for the next turn only. The destination model rereads conversation context when the model changes mid-session.
findings.source_detail: Slash Commands Reference, Configuration and messaging /model entries.
findings.open_question: Exact outbound payload and availability on v0.22.5 remain unverified.

findings.title: Child transcript stays with the launching profile
findings.fact: A profile-routed child uses the target profile’s model, credentials and terminal policy. The child keeps the parent’s toolset and its transcript is stored in the launching profile’s session database.
findings.source_detail: Delegation Provider Plugins, Routes, upstream documentation.
findings.open_question: Which transcript portions are transmitted on a later cloud turn in v0.22.5.

findings.title: Hermes SSH terminal backend uses explicit remote credentials
findings.fact: Upstream documents terminal.backend ssh and SSH host/user/key settings in the Hermes .env file, separating gateway messaging from remote command execution. This is a remote shell capability, not a privilege boundary or sandbox by itself.
findings.source_detail: Network Isolation; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: SSH reachability, least-privilege configuration and isolation depend on the deployment; no end-to-end test was performed.

findings.dimension: Autonomous tool execution and sandbox safety
findings.title: Hermes skips dangerous-command approval in container terminal backends
findings.fact: The v0.22.5 security guide lists Docker as an isolated terminal backend where the dangerous-command check is skipped because the container is the intended boundary. Persistent container mode bind-mounts task workspace and root directories; ephemeral mode uses tmpfs. Explicitly forwarded environment variables can become visible to container code.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5 Security, Container Isolation, Filesystem Persistence, Terminal Backend Security Comparison.
findings.open_question: Host VM/container policy, effective network egress and filesystem isolation for a particular local installation remain unverified.

findings.title: Hermes Python execution defaults to project working directory, not OS isolation
findings.fact: At v0.22.5, execute_code says its sandbox is a security envelope, not an isolation jail. Its default mode is project, running a persistent Python kernel in the session working directory with the project interpreter when active. A check_execute_code_guard call precedes local or remote dispatch; the presence of that guard does not prove filesystem or network isolation.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5 tools/code_execution_tool.py, execute_code, check_execute_code_guard, DEFAULT_EXECUTION_MODE, _get_execution_mode; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: The approval guard's effectiveness under adversarial Python, OS permissions, network egress and actual VM isolation remain untested; strict mode is a temp-directory mode, not proof of a jail.

findings.title: Hermes file-write safety applies to named file tools, not a VM boundary
findings.fact: The v0.22.5 security guide describes a denylist and optional write sandbox for the write_file and patch tools, separately from dangerous-command approval and container isolation. These are distinct controls; the documented file-tool guard alone does not establish confinement of shell or Python code.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5 Security, Overview and File Write Safety; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Complete enforcement and bypass behavior across file tools, symlinks, terminal, Python, plugins and delegated agents requires source-path review and isolated negative testing.

findings.title: Hermes warns against two agents sharing one memory home
findings.fact: The v0.22.5 memory guide cautions that two Hermes agent processes must not point at the same home directory: automatic memory writes can combine entries from both agents into unintended shared state. It recommends separate profiles for separate agents.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5 Persistent Memory, How It Works, One agent per Hermes home.
findings.open_question: This does not establish a cross-process single-writer enforcement mechanism or whether Hermes meets R2's writer-epoch and recovery requirements.

findings.title: Hermes memory writes are automatic unless approval is enabled
findings.fact: In v0.22.5, memory.write_approval defaults to false, permitting memory writes including background self-improvement updates. Setting it true requires approval; noninteractive writes are staged for later review. Both built-in stores can be disabled without disabling external memory provider plugins.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5 Persistent Memory, Configuration and Controlling memory writes (write_approval).
findings.open_question: Actual enforcement under adversarial requests, third-party memory plugins, or R2-style transactional memory semantics has not been independently tested.

findings.title: v0.22.5 documents spoken interruption
findings.fact: The tagged voice guide describes interrupting during generation or playback and saying stop to end the voice conversation.
findings.source_detail: v0.22.5, CLI Voice Mode, Barge-in.
findings.open_question: A built-in spoken provider-change command and measured voice latency remain unverified.

findings.title: Disabling automatic turn retention does not gate built-in memory mirroring
findings.fact: At the examined adapter revision, on_memory_write queues built-in memory add and replace content without checking auto_retain. Remove actions are ignored by this hook. Setting auto_retain false alone therefore does not disable every provider write path.
findings.source_detail: Hindsight integration commit d952b6e655fccab4581ee0722b51c5f103873d12, on_memory_write and _enqueue_retain. October 30 probe used simulated collaborators; source re-inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: No live backend write or network transmission was observed. The installed plugin, active hooks, endpoint location and other controls remain unverified.

findings.title: Hindsight's Hermes recall formatter emits result text
findings.fact: In recall mode, _do_recall joins each result's text into bullet lines. That formatter does not include separate result identifiers or metadata fields, even if a backend result supplies them. Backend storage and the context delivered by this adapter are distinct.
findings.source_detail: Hindsight integration commit d952b6e655fccab4581ee0722b51c5f103873d12, _do_recall; separate reflect mode is outside this claim. October 30 isolated projection probe; source re-inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Text may itself contain attribution. Whether the chosen installation delivers source, approval and supersession information through another path has not been tested.

findings.title: Two wake phrases can select local and cloud assistants
findings.fact: A compatible Assist satellite can map two wake phrases to separate voice pipelines. The project gives an example using one local pipeline and a second cloud-backed pipeline.
findings.source_detail: Voice Chapter 11, multiple wake words and pipelines, introduced in 2025.10.
findings.open_question: Shared conversation history and device-specific compatibility are unverified.

findings.title: A separate Jarvis desktop app supports Linux and LM Studio
findings.fact: The project publishes a Linux x64 package, supports Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers including LM Studio, and documents a fast model for voice intent and tool routing. Its diary and knowledge graph stay on the computer.
findings.source_detail: README, Quick Install, Hardware and model choices, and What you can do. Separate from AI Workshop Jarvis.
findings.open_question: Spoken local/cloud provider switching, multi-agent delegation, and hardware-specific performance remain unverified.

findings.title: Hands-free command selects a named cloud model in the UI
findings.fact: A supplied video inspection report states that the presenter activated hands-free mode and requested Fable 5 by voice. The interface then displayed Claude Fable 5.
findings.source_detail: 1:21–2:28, supplied inspection report.
findings.open_question: Provider request, conversation history and tool data sent on the switch remain unverified.

findings.title: Spoken command changes voice while Qwen remains selected
findings.fact: A supplied video inspection report states that the local voice panel changed while Qwen remained selected.
findings.source_detail: 4:35–7:35, supplied inspection report.
findings.open_question: Offline transcription and synthesis were not independently verified.

findings.title: The creator offers prompts and build instructions
findings.fact: AI Workshop Lite lists Jarvis prompts and build instructions as free community resources.
findings.source_detail: AI Workshop Lite, About, resource list.
findings.open_question: A complete source release, its license, and reproducible installation steps for this exact build on Ubuntu remain unverified.

findings.title: Spoken local model selection appears in the demo
findings.fact: The November 6 video inspection reports a spoken request to switch to the local brain and another to select Gemma. It reports corresponding Qwen and Gemma interface labels and an edit between command and response.
findings.source_detail: 0:00–0:45 and 2:44–4:35. Based on the prior video inspection, not an independent replay today.
findings.open_question: Which endpoint answered, whether any traffic still left the machine, and what history or tool results crossed the switch.

findings.title: User memory can enter each new message
findings.fact: LibreChat documents structured user memory added to message context and an option for an agent to use a separate memory store.
findings.source_detail: User Memory, scope and message context.
findings.open_question: Which memories and earlier tool results are transmitted when moving a specific conversation from a local model to a cloud provider.

findings.title: LibreChat documents a local Ollama endpoint
findings.fact: The project provides endpoint configuration for connecting its self-hosted chat interface to Ollama.
findings.source_detail: Configuration, AI Endpoints, Ollama.
findings.open_question: Whether a spoken request can change providers mid-conversation and how supporting services behave offline.

findings.title: MCP tool annotations require a trusted source
findings.fact: The MCP 2025-11-25 Tools specification requires clients to treat tool annotations as untrusted unless they come from trusted servers. Tools have input schemas and may supply output schemas; when supplied, server structured results must conform and clients should validate them.
findings.source_detail: Protocol revision 2025-11-25, Tool and Output Schema sections; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Schema conformity does not prove factual correctness or permission to act. No deployed tool, sandbox, annotation trust policy or output validation path was tested.

findings.title: OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs pass conversation history by default
findings.fact: The Agents SDK handoff transfers control to the receiving specialist, which sees the existing conversation history unless the application configures an input filter or history mapper. Handoff metadata alone does not replace or restrict that history.
findings.source_detail: Handoffs — Creating a handoff, Input filters and history behavior; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: Exact information revealed by any installed agent depends on its history filters, provider endpoints and application configuration; no deployed workflow was inspected.

findings.title: Manager-as-tool and handoff patterns have different control ownership
findings.fact: OpenAI's SDK documents agents-as-tools as a manager retaining control and combining specialist outputs, while handoffs make the selected specialist the active agent for the remainder of the turn. Code-defined orchestration is supported alongside LLM-chosen routing.
findings.source_detail: Agent orchestration — Core SDK patterns, Orchestrating via LLM and Orchestrating via code; inspected November 7, 2026.
findings.open_question: These documented primitives do not prove one design improves coding correctness, cost or sandbox security without comparable executed benchmarks.

findings.title: The gateway assumes mutually trusted operators
findings.fact: The security guide defines one trust boundary per gateway and calls for separate gateways and credentials for mixed-trust operation.
findings.source_detail: Security, One trust boundary per gateway.
findings.open_question: What filesystem and outbound network access a particular deployment permits.

findings.title: OpenClaw documents LM Studio and Ollama backends
findings.fact: OpenClaw can connect to a separately managed local model server. Its guide distinguishes a short chat reply from a successful tool call under the agent’s full prompt.
findings.source_detail: Local models, Hardware floor and Pick a backend.
findings.open_question: Tool reliability, context capacity and latency on particular local hardware remain unverified.

findings.title: A non-default session model can fail closed
findings.fact: The active session can switch models while retaining its transcript. An explicitly selected non-default model fails visibly when unreachable. Selecting the effective default clears that pin and permits configured fallbacks.
findings.source_detail: Models CLI, user session selection and /model in chat.
findings.open_question: Whether speech can select the model and whether tool or memory services independently contact a cloud provider.
